clue.text: Beastly play given to trouble on foot with nothing had trouble with everything

parts.note: taken as written; 'given to' just supplies the word to
trouble or fuss is ado
nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so the word had is jumbled

parts.note: everything is all

explanation.surface: A theatre review grumbling that a play about an animal caused foot trouble and general trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had trouble' gives ADH, the anagram of HAD. 'Beastly' points to the animal hero: this is A. A. Milne's stage version of The Wind in the Willows.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne's stage adaptation of The Wind in the Willows, whose characters are animals, hence a beastly drama.

clue.text: See 9
Accumulate alleged value of Paris

definitions.meaning: to accumulate is to gather together, pile up
King Henri IV of France is said to have declared Paris well worth a Mass when he converted to Catholicism

explanation.walkthrough: Henri IV is reported to have said 'Paris vaut bien une messe' (Paris is well worth a Mass), so 'alleged' marks the saying as attributed.
explanation.definitionFit: To accumulate is to gather up; separately, the price Henri IV reportedly paid for the city was a religious service.

clue.text: End of the world between two poles arranged by veterans

indicators.note: between means the last letter of world sits inside the rearranged poles
arranged means the letters of those two poles are rearranged

parts.note: two copies of the word pole

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of world

explanation.surface: An expedition from pole to pole, the end of the world, organised by old soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns POLEPOLE into OLPEOPLE, and the D from the end of 'world' goes inside it, giving OL-D-PEOPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Veterans are those who have lived a long time, the elderly.

clue.text: Huge loss

definitions.meaning: the liner that sank in 1912 was a famous loss at sea

explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means gigantic, and the great liner of that name was lost on its maiden voyage.

clue.text: A part (keeping monarch back) of space in a waistcoat

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so role contains the turned monarch

parts.note: an actor's part is a role

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation for monarch is read in reverse

parts.note: HM is short for His or Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A theatrical part, with the king held back, in a waistcoat scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the monarch's abbreviation before it is held inside the actor's part. HM is His or Her Majesty.
explanation.definitionFit: The armhole is the opening in a sleeveless garment like a waistcoat through which the arm passes.

clue.text: Met man that might have been a crowd?

definitions.text: Met man that might have been a crowd?

parts.words: Met man that might have been a crowd?
parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police; Sir Hugh (surname Orde), a candidate to lead it, gives a word for a throng once his initial is set before the surname

explanation.walkthrough: The Met is London's Metropolitan Police; in 2011 Sir Hugh (surname Orde) was a candidate to be its Commissioner. 'Met man' tempts toward a weatherman or an opera singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde is a large crowd or throng of people.

clue.text: Take care of dish with a foot in it

indicators.note: in it means the following pieces go inside the word for an attractive person

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person, a looker

explanation.surface: Instructions for minding a dish that has a foot stuck in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To look after something is to tend it, a phrasal synonym of taking care of it.

clue.text: Crime brings one of her own to Germany

parts.note: Germany's own woman is a Frau, the German for a married woman
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A crime story in which a country gets back one of its own women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'her' refers to Germany, so 'one of her own' is a German woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraud is criminal deception carried out for gain.

clue.text: The shepherd's farewell directs us now towards poet's dream of sorrow then

indicators.note: to direct is to arrange or order, so the words that follow are put in a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is dropped and all five letters p-o-e-t-s are used

explanation.surface: A farewell from a shepherd steering us toward a poet's sorrowful vision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'directs' rearranges all 34 letters of 'us now towards poet's dream of sorrow then'. The line closes Milton's Lycidas, an elegy spoken by a shepherd.
explanation.definitionFit: The last line of Milton's pastoral elegy Lycidas, where the shepherd singer departs, is a famous parting phrase.

clue.text: Aim to share points with 1 across, maybe, to attract following of retired artist

indicators.note: following means the word for attract comes after the other pieces

parts.note: the answer to 1 across is a stage work, an example of a play

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn backwards, so the little word of is reversed

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
to draw is to attract

explanation.surface: A team trying to share points with a play, hoping to win over a retired painter.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 across, maybe' points to Toad of Toad Hall as an example of a play. 'retired' reverses the little word of, and 'following' puts the word for attract last.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing for a draw means settling for a tied result, where each side takes a share of the points.

clue.text: Artist with record rendering of stone

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
rendered into German, stone is Stein

explanation.surface: An artist with a recording of a stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rendering' means translating: the German word for stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob Epstein was a sculptor, an artist who worked in stone and bronze.

clue.text: Monarch in cricket ground left for protection

indicators.note: in means the monarch goes inside the cricket ground

parts.note: the Oval is a London cricket ground
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A monarch at a cricket ground leaves for safety.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a Test cricket ground in south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Overalls are protective work clothing worn over other clothes.

clue.text: Half mature folk smothered in sauce have been brought before the bench

indicators.note: smothered in means placed inside the sauce

parts.note: HP is a British brand of brown sauce

indicators.note: half means only the first three of the six letters of the word for grown-ups are kept

parts.note: mature folk are adults

explanation.surface: Grown-ups half drowned in sauce, then taken to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' keeps ADU of ADULTS. HP Sauce is a common British brown sauce; 'have been' joins the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To be had up is British informal for being charged and taken to court before magistrates.

clue.text: Punishment for 10 times 10 times half 10, otherwise 10 divided by 10 and 10

parts.note: ten times ten times five is 500, the Roman numeral D

indicators.note: otherwise means put another way, so the three spelt-out tens are rearranged
divided by means the first ten is broken up, its letters split apart by the other pieces

parts.note: 10 spelt out is ten
10 spelt out is ten
the figures 1 and 0 look like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A teacher's sum about tens set as an arithmetic punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: '10 times 10 times half 10' is 500, Roman D. The setter means 'otherwise' to reorder one ten as ETN, then 'divided by' splits it with another ten and with IO (the figures 1 0 as letters).
explanation.definitionFit: Detention is a school punishment of being kept in after hours.

clue.text: Subject of mutual attraction?

parts.note: a school science dealing with how atoms bond, also the spark between two people who are drawn to each other

explanation.definitionFit: The science studies bonding between atoms, and the word also means the spark between two people.

clue.text: Impossible to get home with the sun turning blue

parts.note: at home is in
Sol is the Latin name for the sun

indicators.note: turning means the letters of blue are rearranged

explanation.surface: Unable to get home because the sun turned blue.
explanation.definitionFit: An insoluble problem cannot be solved, so it is impossible.

clue.text: Awkwardly placed for penalty?

parts.note: a phrase meaning put in a difficult position, also where the ball sits for a penalty kick

explanation.definitionFit: Being put in an awkward position is the idiom; the penalty mark is a literal spot.

clue.text: Subject of drugs?

definitions.meaning: a subject of study, the science of matter and energy
physic is an old word for medicine

explanation.definitionFit: It is a school subject, and old usage calls a medicine a physic, so its plural means medicines.

clue.text: Marker on the water in French still life

parts.note: a tab is a marker on a file or page
French for the water is l'eau

explanation.surface: A marker floating on the water in a French painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a motionless group or scene, a picture held still.

clue.text: With sound reduced by revolving doors

indicators.note: revolving means turning round, so the letters of doors are shuffled

explanation.walkthrough: SORDO is an Italian musical direction meaning muted.
explanation.definitionFit: In music sordo is a direction to play muted, with the volume damped.

clue.text: I leave homework to unpleasant family rulers

indicators.note: leave means the letter I goes out

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is work on the home
unpleasant means nasty

explanation.surface: Someone abandoning their housework to a horrid royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynasty is a line of rulers from the same family.

clue.text: Fight for very little

explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is informally a fight, and also a tiny fragment of something.

clue.text: Throwback to one going through the country

parts.note: a lob is a throw, so throw back gives lob read in reverse
one is I in Roman numerals
via means going by way of

explanation.surface: A throwback to someone passing through the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throwback' looks like one word but works as throw (LOB) plus back, giving BOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolivia is a South American country, an example of a nation.

clue.text: 5 to 9 points for the earth mother

parts.note: V is 5 in Roman numerals
IX is 9 in Roman numerals
E and N are compass points

explanation.surface: Scoring five to nine points for an earth goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earth' is a fox's den, so the mother there is a female fox.
explanation.definitionFit: A vixen is a female fox, the mother of cubs in an earth, as a fox's den is called.

clue.text: Debilitating condition of setter hiding a very small quantity

indicators.note: hiding means holding the other pieces inside

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me
a means one, the Roman numeral I
a grain is a very small quantity

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler concealing a tiny amount of a disabling illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A migraine is a severe headache that can leave sufferers unable to function.

clue.text: Dog with shorts?

parts.note: a breed of dog, and also a fighter in the ring who wears shorts

explanation.definitionFit: A boxer is a breed of dog, and a boxer in the ring wears shorts.

clue.text: See 9
